pipe_puzzles.title: The Alchemist's Shelf
pipe_puzzles.brief: The potion shelf is a mess. Emit the potions in alphabetical order.
pipe_puzzles.hint: One command sorts lines: sort potions.txt

pipe_puzzles.title: Duplicate Runes
pipe_puzzles.brief: The scribe copied runes twice. Emit each rune once, sorted.
pipe_puzzles.input:
kenaz
algiz
kenaz
dagaz
algiz
kenaz
pipe_puzzles.hint: uniq only removes ADJACENT duplicates — sort first: sort runes.txt | uniq (or sort -u)

pipe_puzzles.title: The Warden's Tally
pipe_puzzles.brief: Count how many of each monster was slain (sorted alphabetically, uniq -c format).
pipe_puzzles.input:
ghoul
wraith
ghoul
imp
ghoul
wraith
pipe_puzzles.hint: sort kills.txt | uniq -c   — uniq -c prefixes each line with its count

pipe_puzzles.title: Greatest Treasures
pipe_puzzles.brief: From the loot ledger, emit the TWO most common items, most common first (uniq -c format).
pipe_puzzles.input:
emerald
gold-coin
emerald
silver-ring
emerald
gold-coin
pipe_puzzles.hint: Chain it: sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 2

pipe_puzzles.title: The Ledger's Second Column
pipe_puzzles.brief: The ledger is comma-separated: item,gold. Emit ONLY the gold values, in file order.
pipe_puzzles.hint: cut -d, -f2 ledger.txt   — -d sets the delimiter, -f picks the field

pipe_puzzles.title: SHOUT THE INCANTATION
pipe_puzzles.brief: The spell only works in uppercase. Transform the whole scroll.
pipe_puzzles.input:
by ash and ember
the gate shall open
pipe_puzzles.target:
BY ASH AND EMBER
THE GATE SHALL OPEN
pipe_puzzles.hint: tr reads piped input: cat whisper.txt | tr a-z A-Z

pipe_puzzles.title: Redact the True Name
pipe_puzzles.brief: Saying the demon's name summons it. Replace every 'morgul' with 'REDACTED'.
pipe_puzzles.input:
morgul rose at dusk
we fled from morgul
morgul cannot cross water
pipe_puzzles.target:
REDACTED rose at dusk
we fled from REDACTED
REDACTED cannot cross water
pipe_puzzles.hint: sed 's/old/new/' replaces the first match per line — no g flag needed here (one name per line)

pipe_puzzles.title: How Many Sightings?
pipe_puzzles.brief: Emit ONLY the number of lines that mention 'ghost' (just the number).
pipe_puzzles.input:
day 1: a ghost in the cellar
day 2: quiet
day 3: ghost again, by the altar
day 4: rats
day 5: the ghost sang
pipe_puzzles.hint: grep -c counts matching lines: grep -c ghost journal.txt

pipe_puzzles.title: The Grand Pipeline
pipe_puzzles.brief: From the roster, emit the sorted, unique CLASSES (second ,-field) of entries that contain 'elf'.
pipe_puzzles.input:
elf,ranger
dwarf,smith
elf,mage
human,knight
elf,ranger
half-elf,bard
pipe_puzzles.hint: Three links: grep elf roster.txt | cut -d, -f2 | sort -u

pipe_puzzles.title: Number the Verses
pipe_puzzles.brief: Emit the first three lines of the epic, each numbered (nl format).
pipe_puzzles.input:
the blade was forged
in mountain fire
and cooled in tears
of those who fell
pipe_puzzles.target:
1  the blade was forged
2  in mountain fire
3  and cooled in tears

hunt_scenarios.title: The Lost Amulet
hunt_scenarios.brief: Somewhere in these chambers a note reveals where the amulet is buried. Find the text that mentions 'amulet' and read it.
hunt_scenarios.hint: grep -r amulet .   searches every file under the current room

files./hunt/chapel/prayer.txt: guard us from what sleeps below
files./hunt/crypt/epitaph.txt: here lies the keeper of the amulet — SIGIL{amulet-beneath-the-yew}

hunt_scenarios.title: A Key With No Door
hunt_scenarios.brief: One file in these vaults ends in `.key`. Find it by NAME, then read it.
hunt_scenarios.hint: find . -name "*.key"   — quote the pattern so the shell doesn't expand it first

hunt_scenarios.title: The Hidden Shrine
hunt_scenarios.brief: The monks hid their shrine as a dotfile. Reveal what normal eyes cannot see, and read it.
hunt_scenarios.hint: ls -a shows dotfiles; find . -name ".*" -type f hunts them everywhere

hunt_scenarios.title: The Deep Archive
hunt_scenarios.brief: The record you need is buried levels deep and mentions 'dragon'. Combine your search spells.
hunt_scenarios.hint: grep -rl dragon .   lists WHICH files match — then cat the one it names

files./hunt/stacks/row-i/shelf-a/tome-2.txt: wyverns are lesser drakes, properly speaking
files./hunt/stacks/row-ii/shelf-b/tome-3.txt: the last dragon left one scale — SIGIL{scale-of-the-first-flame}

hunt_scenarios.title: The Case of the Cloak
hunt_scenarios.brief: A witness wrote the thief's description, but nobody recalls the letter-case. Search for 'CLOAK' in any case.
hunt_scenarios.hint: grep -ri cloak .   — the -i flag ignores case

files./hunt/reports/tuesday.txt: a figure in a CloAk fled east — SIGIL{crimson-hem-torn}

cards.why: chmod changes a file's mode; +x adds the execute bit.

cards.q: Run the executable script named ritual in THIS directory
cards.why: The ./ prefix means 'right here' — without it the shell only searches $PATH.

cards.q: List the room showing file types (executables get a *)
cards.why: -F appends a type marker: / for dirs, * for executables, @ for links.

cards.q: Show permissions, owner, and size for every file, including hidden ones
cards.why: -l is long form (permissions first column), -a includes dotfiles.

cards.q: Create a symbolic link named portal pointing to /entrance
cards.why: ln -s TARGET NAME forges a soft link — a signpost to another path.

cards.q: Set an environment variable HP to 30 (visible to child programs)
cards.why: export marks the variable for every command you run afterwards.

cards.q: Print the value of the variable I
cards.why: $NAME expands to the variable's value inside a command line.

cards.q: Add 'sword' to the front of inventory variable I, keeping what was there
cards.why: The old value expands inside the new one — this is how bashcrawl treasure works.
env dumps the whole spellbook of the current session.

cards.q: Subtract 5 from HP using shell arithmetic
cards.why: let evaluates arithmetic; the game's combat damage works exactly like this.
wc -l counts lines; piping cat into wc teaches the same idea.

cards.q: Show only the first 5 lines of scroll
cards.why: head shows the start of a file; -n picks how many lines.

cards.q: Sort tome.txt and drop duplicate lines with ONE command
cards.why: -u (unique) folds duplicates after sorting — shorthand for sort | uniq.

cards.q: Save the output of ls into a file named manifest
cards.why: > redirects a command's output into a file (overwriting it).

cards.q: Append the word 'done' to the file log.txt
cards.why: >> appends instead of overwriting — the file keeps its history.
pwd stands for "Print Working Directory" - it shows your

cards.q: Seeing What's Around You — which command?
cards.why: ls stands for "List" - it reveals the contents of your current room.
cd stands for "Change Directory" - it moves you from room to room.

cards.q: Print Working Directory - shows your exact location
List files and directories in current location
List with type indicators: * = executable, / = directory, @ = link
List ALL files including hidden (.), with permissions and details
Search for pattern in all files recursively
